stages.title: Plan, order & shop setup
stages.summary: Lock in every option that is hard to add later, confirm the BluePrint accessory drive, and set up the shop before the truck arrives. FFR assigns a completion date at order; the SEMA special (Nov 2026) gives $2,500 off the kit or $3,500 off options.
stages.manual: General Information chapter: tools list, torque and fluid specs.

reads.label: Power Surge Coupe #692, pages 1–2 (a current order sheet)
Solid Car Guys Ep 4: Build School instructors

challenges: Options that cannot be added later: IRS, power steering, A/C kit, hydraulic clutch, windows, wipers, powder coat, EFI in-tank fuel.
Pin-drive wheels do not work with the IRS (Jeff Kleiner). Stick with bolt-on Halibrands.
BluePrint's package says STOP AND CALL for Factory Five fitment: confirm the front drive carries both an A/C compressor and a PS pump.
Two TKX/IRS driveshafts are listed (60175 at 10.50" vs 16038 at 8.38"). Call FFR with the BluePrint bellhousing/TKX length.
ideas: Start a parts-and-cost spreadsheet like Yellville's on day one.
Take the Mk5 Roadster Build School before the kit ships; FFR says Gen 3 coupe builders take that class.
Post on the ffcars Northwest board for a Puget Sound coupe owner who will let you sit in a finished car. Seat fit and headroom cannot be judged from photos.
tasks: Get a written FFR quote with every option line
Call FFR: which TKX/IRS driveshaft fits the BluePrint bellhousing
Call BluePrint: A/C front drive with PS pump bracket
Sit in a finished Gen 3 coupe (seat and headroom check)
Place the kit order and record the completion date
Start Hagerty under-construction coverage on delivery
Set up the shop: lift or stands, body dolly, bench, lighting

stages.title: Delivery & inventory
stages.summary: The body ships on top of the chassis and needs four people to lift off. Missing or wrong hardware is normal: photograph every box and email partsales@factoryfive.com within days. Put the MSO and every receipt in a binder; Washington's inspection depends on them.
stages.manual: Disassembly of the Kit chapter: unboxing and parts check-off.

reads.label: First FFR build – Gen 3 Coupe, page 1 (veteran inventory advice)
Power Surge #692 on missing hardware at delivery

challenges: Backordered quarter windows and side windows are common late ships; log backorders in writing within 30 days.
The quarter-window areas of the body need the most bodywork (edwardb).
The name on the MSO must match the titling applicant. WSP requires the original.
ideas: Build a body dolly first.
Store aluminum panels flat and labeled; they dent and oxidize in storage.
tasks: Photograph every box before opening
Check the packing list against the order form
Email partsales@ about missing or wrong parts within days
Lift the body off (4 people) onto the dolly
Put the MSO and all receipts in the binder
Label and store aluminum panels flat

stages.title: Chassis prep & aluminum panels
stages.summary: The biggest single job: hundreds of holes drilled, cleco'd, riveted and sealed. Heat shielding, firewall insulation and footbox sealing foam go in now, before the body is on and the firewall corner fills with hoses.
stages.manual: Chassis Assembly chapter: aluminum panel sections (floors, footboxes, firewall, trunk, cockpit sides).

reads.label: Walton Racing: rivets, clecos and rivnuts
FFR official: chassis aluminum and wiring (Dan Golub)

challenges: Silicone vs Sikaflex debate; panels oxidize if uncoated, so coat them before the pedal box and wiring go in.
Most cockpit heat is engine-bay air pushed along the footbox-to-body gap, not conduction. Seal it with dense foam before the body goes on.
Dropped floors for tall drivers must be decided before panels are riveted.
ideas: Satin clear over aluminum (jgray) for a finished look at low cost.
Standoff aluminum heat shield with an air gap at the headers.
Avoid tar-based mats near heat; they melt and make a sticky mess.
tasks: Inspect powder coat; touch up bare spots
Fit, drill and cleco every aluminum panel
Install footbox heat shields and firewall insulation
Seal the footbox-to-body gap with dense foam
Rivet and seal panels (Sikaflex every seam)
Spray or lay sound deadening before carpet areas close

stages.title: Front suspension, steering, pedals & brakes
stages.summary: KONI coil-overs, the Wilwood pedal box and the steering column go in while the footbox is open. Decide power steering, quick-release wheel and pedal spacing now. FFR itself says you will want power steering once you try manual.
stages.manual: Chassis Assembly: front suspension, steering rack and column, pedal box, brake lines.

reads.label: Low Boost Films: Wilwood pedal box install
Quick release + Russ Thompson turn signal

challenges: Accelerator pedal vs steering-shaft interference (Bob Brandle made a spacer); throttle pedal wobble (jgray).
Standard 500 lb front springs may be light if the finished car tops 2,900 lb.
A cast Wilwood clutch pedal broke on a roadster with a cable clutch; hydraulic lowers the load.
ideas: Dead-pedal kit and rigid stainless brake lines (edwardb).
Bench-bleed, then pressure-bleed at 5–7 psi.
tasks: Assemble and install front control arms and spindles
Install KONI coil-overs and front sway bar
Mount the pedal box; set pedal height and dead pedal
Install steering rack, column and quick-release hub
Install front brakes and run hard lines
Bench-bleed master cylinders

stages.title: Rear suspension (IRS) & rear brakes
stages.summary: The 2015 Mustang-based IRS is the street choice: smoother ride, better traction, and nearly impossible to retrofit. It needs its own shocks (17150), the 2018 3.55 center section (16668) and the matching driveshaft.
stages.manual: Chassis Assembly: rear suspension (IRS supplement), e-brake.

reads.label: The Roadster Experience: FFR IRS install (same IRS as the coupe)
Grassroots Motorsports Gen 3 race build (IRS assembly)

challenges: IRS bushing misalignment needs spacers; drill spindle and mount holes to 5/8".
Pinion flange adapter error that FFR replaced (P100DHG #138).
Ask about 3.73 vs 3.55 for the TKX 0.81 overdrive.
ideas: Electric parking brake (Levy Racing / Wilwood EPB) frees the tunnel.
Torque-seal every fastener for the inspector.
tasks: Assemble IRS cradle, knuckles and hubs
Install center section and CV axles
Install rear coil-overs and sway bar
Install rear brakes and parking brake
Install driveshaft and safety loop
Torque-seal every fastener

stages.title: Engine & transmission
stages.summary: BluePrint 347 EFI (Holley Sniper 2, 415 hp) with the TKX. The package already includes a McLeod hydraulic throw-out bearing, so order FFR #34158 (master kit) and not #16427. The TKX shifter lands too far back in a Gen 3: flip it 180° or buy a mid-shift kit.
stages.manual: Chassis Assembly: engine and transmission install, driveshaft, mounts, headers and side exhaust, cooling.

reads.label: GT_Rich 427 SBF Coupe R (TKX, built in 7 months)
EFI for BluePrint engine (Art Shand, Sniper cold-start)
GAS-N Gen 3 headers: new option thread
Gen 3 Coupe FAQ (small-block is better for footroom)

challenges: TKX shifter position; several builders flipped the shifter and moved the tunnel hole.
Oil pan clearance (rear-sump), tall intakes hit the hood, degas/overflow tank location.
The 4-into-2-into-sidepipe routing is a reported power robber; GAS-N's design has a longer, more gradual turn.
ideas: Ceramic headers and standoff heat shields; bare FFR pipes rust fast in Washington.
Fan shroud (Breeze 70807) for low-speed and A/C idle cooling.
Driveshaft safety loop on rivnuts.
tasks: Set engine and trans on the mounts
Check oil-pan and intake clearance
Install hydraulic clutch and bleed
Fit shifter position (flip or mid-shift kit)
Install headers and side pipes; check heat shields
Install radiator, fan, shroud and hoses

stages.title: Wiring, fuel, hydraulics & gauges
stages.summary: Ron Francis harness, in-tank EFI pump, hydraulic clutch and brake lines, battery in the nose. Plan the crowded firewall corner where harness, heater hoses and A/C lines all meet.
stages.manual: Chassis Assembly: wiring harness, fuel tank and EFI in-tank pump, radiator and fan, clutch hydraulics, gauges.

reads.label: FFR chassis harness manual (Rev W, PDF)
Walton Racing: first start and wiring lessons
Sniper EFI fuel pump vs FF in-tank

challenges: BluePrint ECU/injector data mismatch (lewma); a wrong control pack cost Walton Racing months.
The Sniper 1 internal regulator is a known failure point; Sniper 2 needs a separate regulator and 3/8" lines.
GPS gauge part number differs between the order form (60312) and catalog (60311).
ideas: Keyless push-button start, all-LED lighting with electronic flashers, GPS speedometer, laser-etched switch panel (edwardb).
Door-pocket phone chargers (Rocky R.), one aux lead straight to the battery for a tender.
tasks: Mount battery, cutoff switch and bus bar
Route the Ron Francis harness; plan the firewall corner
Install in-tank fuel pump, regulator and lines
Wire the Sniper ECU, O2 sensor and inertia switch
Install gauges and switch panel
Install lighting and test every circuit

stages.title: A/C, heater & defroster
stages.summary: Space behind the Gen 3 dash is tight; edwardb concluded the FFR kit (Siroco Boreal 600) is the best and maybe only solution. As delivered it has two always-on outlets and no defrost diverter. Washington rain plus the WSP defroster check makes this the biggest comfort and inspection risk.
stages.manual: A/C-heater-defroster supplement Rev G: evaporator, condenser, bulkhead fittings, hoses, ducts, wiring, footbox panels.

reads.label: FFR Gen 3 A/C-heater-defroster manual Rev G (PDF)
Heating and A/C options (FFR vs Old Air vs Vintage Air)
Low Boost Films: Vintage Air install in a coupe
P100DHG #138: 90° bulkhead fittings to clear a small-block

challenges: Small evaporator means adequate, not strong, cooling; the hatch glass heat-soaks the cabin.
SBF needs 90° bulkhead fittings; decide footbox heat outlets early.
FFR says have a shop crimp the #6/#8/#10 lines (Mastercool 71550).
ideas: Y-connections feeding 2 defrost + 4 dash outlets (ffcars builder, 4+ seasons without fogging).
Tint the hatch glass; heated seat pads (30-minute install).
tasks: Mount the evaporator in the passenger footbox
Mount condenser ahead of the radiator
Install compressor and belt; check PS pump clearance
Run bulkhead fittings and hoses (90° for SBF)
Plumb heater hoses and control valve
Build the defrost path; have lines crimped and charged

stages.title: Go-kart: first start & first drive
stages.summary: First drive without the body. Weigh the car now to choose spring rates; Gen 3 coupes run well over FFR's 2,400 lb figure (one owner: 2,992 lb wet). Driving in gelcoat for a season is common and finds fit problems before paint.
stages.manual: Chassis Assembly end-of-chapter checklist before go-kart.

reads.label: MJS coupe: first-start debugging and A/C charging
Derek R.'s Type 65 (kit Oct 2021, go-kart in 6 months)

challenges: Brake bias and residual valves; clutch bleed; leaks at every fitting.
Expect Sniper cold-start enrichment tuning.
ideas: Film it. This is the milestone Coco will remember.
tasks: Fill fluids; check for leaks at every fitting
First start; Sniper learn and cold-start tuning
Bleed brakes and clutch; set bias
First drive without the body
Weigh the car on corner scales
Film it

stages.title: Body fit: doors, hood, hatch, windows, lights
stages.summary: The coupe-specific job: door gaps, hatch glass, roof line and side windows take far longer than on a roadster. Bodies vary up to 1/2" side to side. Set hatch glass height and door gaps before paint.
stages.manual: Body chapter: mounting, door hinges and latches, hood, hatch and glass, side windows, wipers, lights, bumpers.

reads.label: John Nizman: body fit and hatch glass
John Nizman: side glass and brackets
Side window question (frames differ side to side)
Tim Custer: Forma power window kit install
Kevin's Garage: setting the body (Mk4, transfers)

challenges: Plastic latch housings crack; add door poppers as a backup and metal handles.
Hood hinge bracket clearance; hatch glass high at the corners (use a temporary D-seal to save the FFR strip).
No Gen 3 builder has documented a fully weather-tight coupe. Plan on FormaCars windows or careful sealing.
ideas: Nose pop-up mod with a BMW E30 hood latch (ffr48).
Quick-release wheel for easier entry; roof NACA ducts if you skip A/C.
tasks: Set the body on the chassis and check gaps
Hang doors; adjust hinges and latches
Fit hood and hatch; set hatch glass height
Install side windows and quarter windows
Install wipers, lights, mirrors
Install weatherstrip; hose test for leaks

stages.title: Title in gelcoat (Washington)
stages.summary: Title before paint so the deadline does not depend on the paint shop. Kit vehicle under RCW 46.12.695: WSP VIN inspection by appointment with the MSO, original receipts, a certified weight slip and the licensing-agent request form. No emissions test in Washington since 2020.
stages.manual: Not in the FFR manual. See the WSP kit vehicle guide and the titling section of the build plan.

reads.label: WSP Assembled Vehicle guide, R 10/25 (newer format; no copies or screenshots)
RCW 46.37.518: hoods and bumpers optional on kit vehicles
Latest experience with WA registration (use tax, 1965 model year)

challenges: Online WSP slots fill in seconds; call the local WSP office. Allow 1–3 months.

Use tax is owed at titling on anything you did not pay Washington sales tax on (~$4,000 in one case). Most big remote sellers collect WA tax at checkout now; private-party and small-shop buys usually don't. Keep every receipt with the tax line visible; the hub's tax-paid flag tracks it.

Bumpers: the WSP checklist lists them, but RCW 46.37.518 makes hoods and bumpers optional on kit vehicles. Make sure the car goes through as a kit vehicle (RCW 46.12.695), not an assembled vehicle, and bring the statute.
ideas: Print RCW 46.37.518 and RCW 46.12.695 for the inspection folder.
Register as a collector vehicle; ask for the 1965 model-year precedent.
Order the extra side mirror (12079X/15834X) for the inspection.
tasks: Get the WSP inspection request form from DOL
Sort receipts: WA sales tax paid vs not (use tax due)
Get a certified weight slip
Book the WSP appointment (call the local office)
Pass inspection; get the VIN assigned
Title and register within 60 days
Collector or regular registration decided

stages.title: Body prep, paint & livery
stages.summary: Coupes need more blocking than roadsters (roof, hatch, jambs). Shops take 3–5 months; budget $8k–$20k+. Vinyl will not go over raw gelcoat, so a wrap is an addition to bodywork, not a substitute.
challenges: Inconsistent gelcoat (GT_Rich); set hatch glass and door gaps before paint.
Doing paint before titling makes the deadline depend on the paint shop.
ideas: Bristol Grey with navy leather (SATA/Hatcher coupe), Blu Avio over Wimbledon White (Rocky R.), bare-aluminum look with period decals (Rob M.).
Partial wraps (roof, stone guards, spats) in 3M PPF hold up fine for ~$200.
tasks: Set door gaps and hatch glass before paint
Choose shop; get a written quote and timeline
Deliver the car in gelcoat
Approve color and livery
Collect the painted car; inspect

stages.title: Interior, insulation, seats & dash
stages.summary: Exhaust is the dominant noise (stock side pipes ~114 dB inside), so quiet pipes matter more than insulation. Seat drop and pedal placement solve headroom for a 6'2" driver; mount seats to the floor, not tracks, to gain 1–1.5".
stages.manual: Final Assembly chapter: carpet, seats and belts, dash, console, weatherstrip, mirrors.

reads.label: Will I physically fit in a Type 65

challenges: The rear diagonal brace limits seat travel; the rear blind spot is real.
edwardb's Corbeaus suit 5'10"; one builder could not make a Corbeau fit the driver's side and went back to FFR seats.
ideas: Leather-wrapped dash over closed-cell foam; removable gauge panel on rivnuts; hidden tablet or Alpine head unit with backup camera; single low LED for night cabin light.
tasks: Lay carpet and sills
Mount seats (floor or track) and belts
Finish dash, gauges and glovebox
Install headliner and door cards
Install audio, camera and USB
Final trim and weatherstrip check

stages.title: Shakedown, alignment & corner balance

groups.label: Which kit
groups.tradeoff: The street Complete Kit is $22,990 and every Coupe-R body piece is an option on it. The Coupe-R ($24,990) buys a competition cage, 750/500 lb springs and a fixed race seat, which are the parts a street car does not want.

groups.label: Engine & transmission
groups.tradeoff: BluePrint 347 EFI is the turnkey path with a hydraulic clutch bearing in the box, about $4,500 less than a Coyote package and better footroom at 6'2". The Coyote is the majority Gen 3 choice and sounds the part, but needs different mounts, headers, PS and A/C kits and a tighter footbox. Carb saves $2,200 and gives up cold starts.

groups.label: Front brakes
groups.tradeoff: Wilwood 12.88" ($2,000–2,300) is the near-universal street upgrade and needs 17"+ wheels. The standard 11" PBR brakes are adequate and the only choice with 15s. Levy's 14" kit is for 18"+ wheels and track use.

groups.label: Rear suspension
groups.tradeoff: IRS rides and tracks better and is what nearly every street Gen 3 runs; it costs roughly $3,000 more than the 3-link once you add the center section and shocks. The 3-link is simpler, lighter and fine for a budget or track car, but you can't switch later.

groups.label: Rear brakes
groups.tradeoff: IRS 11.65"/13" keeps the OEM parking brake and costs the least; Wilwood 12.88" rears ($2,299) match the fronts visually and need an electric or MC4 parking brake solution.

groups.label: Differential
groups.tradeoff: The 2018 Mustang 3.55 unit from FFR is the no-donor path and what Ron L. runs. A Torsen ($775, diff only) adds traction for a street car but you still need the FFR carrier parts.

groups.label: Steering
groups.tradeoff: FFR's hydraulic kit (16799) needs a pump on the 347's front drive, which has to share with the A/C compressor; electric assist ($935) avoids that and the belt, at the cost of a less natural feel. Manual is cheapest and FFR warns you'll regret it.

groups.label: Steering wheel
groups.tradeoff: FFR's 14" wheel is included; a 13" Sparco gives more knee room but heavier steering on a manual rack. A quick-release hub helps entry more than any wheel choice.

groups.label: Clutch hydraulics
groups.tradeoff: 34158 ($220) is the only piece you need with the BluePrint package. Tilton and Forte's kits are for builds that don't come with a bearing.

groups.label: Headers
groups.tradeoff: FFR's 302 headers ($order form) are what the side pipes are designed around. GAS-N long-tubes ($1,095+) flow better and route more gracefully but have had months-long shipping delays.

groups.label: Side exhaust
groups.tradeoff: FFR stainless pipes ($1,525) are the default and loud (~114 dB inside). GAS-N Touring (from $1,495) is the quiet drop-in; Boig quieter still but call-to-order. Inserts ($120–160 a side) are the cheap fix for either.

groups.label: Fan & shroud
groups.tradeoff: Breeze 70807 ($99) is made for the FFR fan and this chassis; a SPAL swap buys little and loses the shroud fit.

groups.label: Battery
groups.tradeoff: Odyssey PC925 ($250) is the proven small AGM; Braille B2015 saves 13 lb for about the same money but is a race battery.

groups.label: Fuel system
groups.tradeoff: FFR's in-tank kit (17680, ~$600) is simplest and what most Sniper builders run; the Holley 12-345 module ($335) gives 3/8" lines and a proper bypass regulator for Sniper 2.

groups.label: Gauges
groups.tradeoff: FFR's GPS set ($1,299) is the coupe default and skips the TKX speed-sensor hassle. Speedhut custom is the same gauges with your choices; Dakota Digital is for a custom dash.

groups.label: A/C & heat
groups.tradeoff: FFR's 302/351W kit (~$1,800) is the only one that fits without fabrication; its weak point is defrost. FormaCars HVAC is the one proven alternative but has no public price. Decide before the footbox closes.

groups.label: Side windows
groups.tradeoff: FFR sliders ($549) are what nearly everyone runs and leak a little; FormaCars roll-downs are the Washington-rain answer, cost unknown, and must be done before door finishing.

groups.label: Wipers
groups.tradeoff: FFR's Lucas kit ($499) is marginal on the big windshield but fits; Specialty Power Windows ($376) sweeps better. Either is far easier with the body off.

groups.label: Mirrors
groups.tradeoff: FFR Raydots (included, extra for the pair) pass inspection; BRE's $289 coupe kit is the period-correct upgrade with backing plates.

groups.label: Seats
groups.tradeoff: FFR low-backs give the most headroom for the money; Kirkey ($250 + cover) is thinner still and floor-mounts. Corbeau and Sparco recline but cost headroom. Sit in a car before buying.

groups.label: Belts
groups.tradeoff: The included Simpson 5-point is track-correct; Schroth's ASM 4-point ($325) is the street-friendlier harness.

groups.label: Dash
groups.tradeoff: The aluminum dash is included; wrapping it over foam is the cheap upgrade; carbon ($600) is a look; a custom dash is a project.

groups.label: Wheels
groups.tradeoff: 17" ($1,600–1,900) clears Wilwoods and has the best tire selection. 15" is period-correct but locks you to 11" brakes. 18" ($1,899) is for 14" rotors or a modern stance, with thinner tire choices.

groups.label: Coupe-R look
groups.tradeoff: Scoops, vents, spoiler and canards are all bonded or riveted into the body, so they go on before paint. The hood scoop and footbox vents give most of the look; the splitter and canards are the pieces that scrape and crack on the street.

groups.label: Paint
groups.tradeoff: A shop blocking and painting a coupe runs $8k–20k; doing your own prep can halve it. Title in gelcoat first either way.

groups.label: Insulation
groups.tradeoff: Lizard Skin sprays go on before carpet and are the biggest single comfort gain; butyl mat on footboxes and tunnel is near-universal. Exhaust choice matters more than any of it for noise.

groups.label: Engine mounts
groups.tradeoff: Follows the engine; nothing to decide once the engine is picked.

groups.label: Driveshaft
groups.tradeoff: Length depends on the bellhousing and trans; FFR lists two TKX/IRS shafts, so this is a phone call, not a preference.

warnings.msg: The IRS does not fit pin-drive (knock-off) wheels.
warnings.why: Pin-drive hubs need a narrower track than the IRS and the Gen 3 front spindles give. Jeff Kleiner: "the IRS is not compatible with pin drive width so the only option there is a narrowed solid axle," and the Gen 3 spindles "do not accommodate the narrow pin drive width."
warnings.fix: Stay with bolt-on wheels (FFR Halibrands, Vintage Wheel Works, Forgestar). If you want knock-offs, you need the 3-link with a narrowed axle and Mustang spindles, with worse geometry. Resolve this once your wheel pick is bolt-on.

warnings.msg: PS pump and A/C compressor both hang on the 347's front drive.
warnings.why: BluePrint's standard 347 front drive carries the alternator; the A/C option adds a compressor. A hydraulic PS pump needs its own bracket and pulley position, and nobody has documented all three on the BluePrint drive in a Gen 3.
warnings.fix: Call BluePrint (1-800-483-4263) and ask for the front-drive option with both A/C compressor and PS pump, or switch steering to electric assist (ePowerSteering KIT-26) and skip the pump. Resolve once BluePrint confirms in writing.

warnings.msg: Wilwood 12.88" fronts do not clear 15" wheels.
warnings.why: The 12.88" rotor and Dynapro 6 caliper need a 17" minimum wheel; Wilwood lists 17" minimum for this kit on the Type 65 Coupe.
warnings.fix: Pick 17" or 18" Halibrands, or keep the standard 11" brakes with the 15s.

warnings.why: A 14" rotor plus caliper needs an 18" or 19" wheel.
warnings.fix: Pick 18" Halibrands or Forgestar 19s, or step down to the 12.88" Wilwoods with 17s.

warnings.msg: 14" rotors probably do not clear 17" wheels.
warnings.why: Ron L. runs this brake on 19s; no Gen 3 build shows it on 17s.
warnings.fix: Confirm with Levy Racing before pairing, or go to 18s.

warnings.msg: 12.88" rear Wilwoods do not clear 15" wheels.
warnings.why: Same rotor and caliper size as the fronts; 17" minimum.
warnings.fix: Pick 17" or 18" wheels, or the IRS 11.65" rear brakes.

warnings.msg: The Coyote is tighter at the footbox than a small-block.
warnings.why: FFR's own FAQ says the small-block is the better choice for footroom; the Coyote's width pushes the footbox walls in.
warnings.fix: Sit in a Coyote coupe before ordering if you're over 6 feet. Resolve once you've checked.

warnings.msg: Kirkeys on a seat track cost you headroom.
warnings.why: Tall drivers floor-mount Kirkeys to gain 1–1.5" of headroom; a track puts it back.
warnings.fix: Skip the track (12077) with Kirkeys, or keep the track with FFR seats. Resolve if you've sat in the car and it fits.
warnings.src: Will I physically fit in a Type 65

warnings.msg: The Tilton bearing duplicates the one in the BluePrint package.
warnings.why: BluePrint's 347/TKX package ships with a McLeod hydraulic throw-out bearing; FFR's 34158 master kit is all you need.
warnings.fix: Drop the Tilton bearing unless you're not using the BluePrint package.

warnings.msg: The Coupe-R is a competition chassis: a cage you sit next to without a helmet, 750/500 lb springs, and a fixed race seat.
warnings.why: FFR sells it as an SCCA/NASA wheel-to-wheel chassis. Cage tubes beside an unhelmeted head are a known street hazard even padded; the spring rates are track rates; the high-back seat has no tracks.
warnings.fix: If the look is what you want, order the street Complete Kit and add the Coupe-R aero options (hood scoop and vents, spoiler, ducts, canards). If you want the cage, plan SFI padding, softer springs and a tracked seat, and confirm A/C and side-window fit with FFR.

warnings.msg: Confirm the A/C evaporator and ducts clear the Coupe-R cage before ordering both.
warnings.why: The street A/C kit was designed around the standard chassis; no documented Coupe-R build runs it.
warnings.fix: Email tech@factoryfive.com with both part numbers; ask for a Coupe-R build with A/C.

warnings.msg: Side windows on a Coupe-R: confirm the door-bar and cage clearance.
warnings.why: The Coupe-R is sold without side windows; the cage door bars sit where the window mechanism lives.
warnings.fix: Ask FFR before ordering; FormaCars has not documented a cage car either.

decideLabels.body: Decide before the body goes on

deps.why: Panels and hardware have to be inventoried before anything is drilled.
Footbox and floor panels go in before the pedal box and suspension.
Rear panels and trunk floor before the IRS cradle.
Pedal box and clutch hydraulics before the engine goes in.
Driveshaft and IRS before the trans is final.
Harness routes around the engine and headers.
A/C wiring and the firewall corner share space with the harness.
Evaporator and condenser plumbing is far easier with no body.
Drive it first; find the leaks and fit problems before the body hides them.
WSP inspects a complete, drivable car.
Title in gelcoat so the deadline doesn't depend on the paint shop.
Carpet and seats go in after paint; nothing gets scratched twice.
Alignment and corner balance with the car at final weight.

gates.label: Insulate and seal before the body goes on
steps: Install footbox heat shields and firewall insulation
Seal the footbox-to-body gap with dense foam
Spray or lay sound deadening before carpet areas close
gates.why: Once the body is on, the footbox-to-body gap and the firewall corner are unreachable. Every heat-and-noise regret thread on the coupe traces back to skipping this.

gates.label: A/C, heater and wipers plumbed body-off
steps: Mount the evaporator in the passenger footbox
Run bulkhead fittings and hoses (90° for SBF)
Build the defrost path; have lines crimped and charged
gates.why: FFR: wipers and A/C are 'much easier with the body off.'

gates.label: Windows decided
gates.why: FormaCars roll-downs need door-skin work before door finishing; sliders don't. Decide before the doors are hung.

gates.label: Title first
steps: Pass inspection; get the VIN assigned
gates.why: The WSP certificate is valid 60 days; title before the car leaves for paint.

gates.label: Seat fit confirmed
gates.why: Seat drop and pedal placement decide headroom for a 6'2" driver; mount before carpet.

gates.label: Clutch hydraulics in
steps: Mount the pedal box; set pedal height and dead pedal
gates.why: The master cylinder and line route before the engine blocks access.

plans.title: Cabin comfort plan
plans.intro: The Gen 3 cabin is hot and loud, and every fix goes in before the body does. Four decisions share that one truth. Pick a target, and the plan tells you whether your combination gets there.

targets.label: Weekend cruiser, can talk at 60
targets.desc: Quiet pipes or inserts, butyl mat, footbox shields.

targets.label: Grand tourer, long drives in the rain
targets.desc: Quiet pipes, full spray insulation + MLV, FFR A/C with a defrost path, roll-down windows.

facts: Stock FFR side pipes measured about 114 dB inside; the exhaust is the dominant noise source, more than any insulation choice.
After extensive insulation a coupe still read above 80 dB at cruise (ffcars Planning thread); insulation lowers the floor, it does not make a quiet car.
Most cockpit heat is engine-bay air pushed along the footbox-to-body gap, not conduction; dense foam at that gap beats another layer of mat.
FFR's evaporator has two always-on outlets and no defrost diverter; builders add Y-connections to defrost and dash outlets. Washington's inspection checks the defroster if installed.
Lizard Skin and mat must go on before carpet, and the footbox-to-body gap is unreachable once the body is on.

rows.label: Exhaust
rows.note: Biggest single lever. Inserts are the cheap fix on either FFR or GAS-N pipes.

rows.label: Insulation
rows.note: Spray goes on first, then mat, then MLV under the carpet. Pick more than one.

rows.label: A/C and heat
rows.note: FFR's kit fits; plan the defrost Y-connections. FormaCars is the better-defrost route.

rows.label: Windows
rows.note: Sliders leak a little and seal poorly; roll-downs are the wet-climate answer.

plans.title: Driver fit plan (6'2")
plans.intro: Headroom and legroom in a Gen 3 come from five choices that interact. The rear brace limits seat travel, so the seat choice does most of the work.

targets.label: Fits, helmet optional
targets.desc: Stock-style seat on tracks and a 14" wheel. Comfortable to about 6'0"; a helmet is tight.

targets.label: Fits at 6'2" with a helmet
targets.desc: Thin-shell seat on the floor, small wheel, quick release.

facts: Floor-mounting the seat instead of using the track gains 1 to 1.5 inches of headroom.
FFR's low-back aluminum seats are the ones FFR itself markets for tall drivers; Kirkey's shell is thinner still.
A 13-inch wheel adds knee room; a quick-release hub adds entry room, which matters more in a coupe.
One builder could not make a Corbeau fit the driver's side at all and went back to FFR seats.
Sit in a finished coupe before buying seats; Fredscoupe in Everett offered.

plans.title: Washington rain plan
plans.intro: Nobody has documented a fully weather-tight Gen 3 coupe. How dry and how safe it is in the wet comes down to the windows, the wipers, the defrost path and what you do about the bare steel.

targets.label: Dry days only
targets.desc: Sliders, stock wipers, garage-kept. Fine for summer cruises.

targets.label: Caught in the rain, no drama
targets.desc: Wipers that clear the big windshield, a real defrost path, bulb seals on the doors, coated pipes.

targets.label: Driven in November anyway
targets.desc: Roll-down windows, sealed marine wipers, LED lighting, a rear camera, coated chassis and exhaust.

rows.label: Side windows
rows.note: Sliders leak a little and seal poorly; roll-downs are the wet-climate answer and the only part here you can't add after paint.

rows.label: Wipers
rows.note: FFR's kit is 'OK but marginal' on the coupe's windshield. Marine motors are sealed to IP66.

rows.label: Defrost
rows.note: A fogged windshield is the real rain problem. FFR's kit has two always-on outlets and no diverter; plan the Y-connections or go FormaCars.

extras: Breeze LED headlight and exterior kits
facts: wallace18 stayed dry through two rainstorms with the FFR windows plus added foam and reworked frames, but says it won't match a production car.
Wayne Yoshida (Gen 1 coupe) skipped ceramic coating and the bare pipes rusted in a year.
edwardb runs the Specialty Power Windows wiper kit; builders call the FFR wipers marginal on the big windshield.
The hatch glass heat-soaks the cabin in sun and fogs in rain; tint it and give the defrost a path to it.
Seal the footbox-to-body gap and every panel seam with Sikaflex before the body goes on; water finds the same gaps the heat does.
The coupe's rear blind spot is real; a camera mirror is the common fix and matters more in the wet.
